thread:
arjun: heads-up — i'm putting together a per-org throttle model we can roll out next quarter. goal: clear mapping from free/pro/enterprise -> (monthly token budget, steady rps, burst bucket) + routing priority weights so dedicated capacity favors higher tiers. sketch below, looking for tradeoffs on enforcement point (edge vs central) and telemetry needs.

jessica: +1 we need something predictable for customers. can you paste the sketch?

arjun: sure, rough draft: 
```
# quota mapping (proto)
free: monthly_tokens=1_000_000, steady_rps=2, burst_tokens=200
pro: monthly_tokens=50_000_000, steady_rps=20, burst_tokens=2000
enterprise: monthly_tokens=UNLIMITED, steady_rps=200, burst_tokens=20_000

# routing priority (higher => prefer dedicated)
priority_weight: free=10, pro=50, enterprise=100

# enforcement model options:
# 1) edge enforcement (proxy): fast, low-latency rejects, but counters are local/approx and cross-node sync is hard
# 2) central quota service: single source of truth, consistent counters, slightly higher latency but can issue per-request tokens and support bursts via token-bucket in redis
```

mike: i lean central quota svc. we've hit weird double-counting with proxy-local buckets before (cache expiry => overdraw). also easier for per-org billing reconciliation.

sophia: central sounds right but ops: what about adding a lightweight allowlist on the edge for emergency throttles? (so we don't have to wait on central if redis is flaky)

arjun: agreed — hybrid: central primary; edge as stateless fast-fail fallback using cached leaky-bucket estimates. edge cache ttl 5s, degrade to 1s during incidents.

jessica: how does this interact with per-key vs per-org quotas? e.g., org has multiple API keys for different teams.

arjun: enforcement rules:
- per-key steady_rps enforced at request-level (pre-auth) to stop noisy keys quickly
- per-org monthly_tokens checked at central service for billing and burst accounting
- burst_tokens drawn from per-org bucket first, then per-key fallback if org exhausted (so keys don't starve org budget)

infra-bot: note: redis token-bucket implementation exists under infra/quota-service. supports multi-bucket atomic decrement via lua. current capacity: ~20k qps if sharded, latency ~1-3ms.

mike: routing priority: how do we use priority_weight? proposal: when dedicated pool is at capacity, scheduler chooses candidates proportional to weight, then apply fallback policy (route to hosted smaller model variant or queue).

arjun: yes. real example: with 100 requests and pool capacity 60, enterprise will get ~60 * (weight_enterprise / sum_weights_active). We should clamp per-org max share to avoid a single org starving others.

sophia: telemetry we need for console: current monthly_tokens_used, current_burst_level (available vs consumed), p95 rate-limit-reject latency, and breakdown by model and route. customers want a per-org remaining quota UI and an events list for when they hit soft/hard caps.

jessica: UX for rollouts — can we gate changes to quota caps behind a feature-flagged rollout (canary to 1% of orgs)? also need a console toggle for support to temporarily increase burst_tokens for a given org (audit log required).

arjun: plan:
1) implement central quota enforcement prototype using existing infra/quota-service lua scripts (1 week spike)
2) add lightweight edge cache policy + emergency allowlist (2 weeks)
3) expose telemetry events (quota.used, quota.burst.consume, quota.reject) to datadog + console endpoints (3 weeks)
4) controlled rollout via feature flags + support UI for temporary increases (2 weeks)

mike: action: i'll scope the redis sharding checklist and perf test.

sophia: i'll mock the console screens for remaining quota + burst graph; will add support workflow for temporary increases.

arjun: i'll open the central-proto PR and include the exact token semantics plus e2e tests. tagging @jessica for billing alignment.

jessica: great — please add a brief note on how this maps to pricing lines (free/pro/enterprise) for finance so they can update the billable metrics.

deploy-bot: scheduled: quota-service/prototype deploy to staging at 2026-03-26 18:30 UTC.

arjun: thanks — will follow up with the PR link and a short runbook for incident-mode throttle overrides.

(most replies are short; ping me if you want to be added to the rollout canary list)
